Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Jon: I measured the entrance this morning: 1.2 meters between the posts, with the gate swinging inward. That’s enough for the standard hand truck, but not if someone leaves a bike across the threshold. The rubber stop on the left post is loose, so I’ve put a yellow tag on it rather than trying to fix it before the parts arrive.

Rina: The parts are in the cabinet by the tool board. There are two spare gate stops in the labeled box, plus the short screws we need. I’ll bring the drill on Thursday. If the rain keeps up, though, let’s wait until the concrete beside the post is dry; the new stop won’t hold properly in a damp hole. I can check the forecast before we set a time.

Space 14 is still usable, and there’s a pump beside the entrance if they want to work on the tire here.

The bulb above the wash area flickers once when it starts, then settles. I wrote down the fixture number, L-07, so we can compare it with the maintenance sheet instead of guessing which one needs a replacement.

Rina: The drain grate is clear now. I found a few leaves and one cable tie, but no standing water after the hose test. The floor slopes gently toward the drain, which is good, though the painted arrows are fading near the back rack. I have white floor paint in the shared cupboard; I’ll only use it if the building manager confirms that the shed paint is okay for concrete.

1. Count bikes and compare the total with the board.

Maya: I put the check-in sheet on the clipboard inside the gate. There’s a pen attached with string, and the last page has a box for noting the time and initials. Rina: The delivery driver asked whether packages can be left inside the shed. I told them we don’t use it as a parcel room, because the aisle and fire exit need to stay open. They can call the office from the marked phone number on the gate. A small sealed box for the maintenance team is the only exception, and it goes on the shelf above the tool cabinet, not beside the bikes.

delivery-summary.tsv

Dev: I’ve added that file name to the handover notes so everyone can find the delivery record from the shared drive. It has a date, a route reference, and a short description for each maintenance drop-off. The shed copy is just a printed index; the office keeps the full record. If a delivery is missing from the list, we should check with the office before assuming it was left at the gate.

Maya: The noticeboard is getting crowded, so I moved the lost-property note below the opening hours. There are two gloves in the clear tray, one silver bottle, and a small front light with a cracked clip. None has a name on it. I’ll keep them there through the end of the month, then take the unclaimed items to the office cupboard for the usual collection.

Jon: I also labeled the wall hooks by size: helmets on the top row, locks in the middle, and reusable shopping bags on the bottom. Those hooks are for temporary items, not long-term storage, so please clear anything that’s still there at the end of each week. The grey helmet belongs to the maintenance team and stays on the top hook; it has a white sticker inside the rim.

Rina: Saturday’s forecast looks dry until mid-afternoon, so I’ve penciled in 10:30 for the gate-stop check. If the concrete is still damp when we arrive, we can do the count and light test first, then come back to the stop once it’s dry. I’ll bring the drill and the spare screws, and I’ll leave the floor paint in the cupboard until we hear back from the building manager.
